Subject: PO visibility for Redwood entities & invoice format question

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the intro — we (Acme Supply, Inc.) are getting set up to bill Redwood. A quick note on our side: we ship and invoice against POs issued to three different Redwood legal entities (Redwood Inc., Redwood EU SARL, Redwood Labs LLC). The POs include the entity code in the PO number but we want to confirm how you prefer we present invoices so finance can accurately route and remit.

Two specific questions: 
1) Portal vs email fallback — is it okay if we start by sending invoices to your email intake while we finish portal onboarding, or does Redwood require portal-only for multi-entity vendors? If email is acceptable, what subject/header token do you need so your AP system auto-routes to the correct legal entity?
2) Invoice template — can you confirm whether Redwood prefers a single consolidated invoice that contains multiple PO lines (one per PO/entity), or individual invoice per PO/legal entity? If consolidated, what are the minimum columns you need (PO number per line, entity code, tax breakdown per entity, remit-to info, currency)?

I attached our current invoice layout for reference (acme_current_invoice.pdf). We are aiming to go live on 2027-04-15; is that feasible?

Appreciate any sample layout or quick checklist you can share so we can align our accounting format.

Best,
Priyanka Shah
Billing Manager, Acme Supply, Inc.
T: +1 415-555-0112

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in from Acme. Their question is about multi-entity PO routing and whether we require portal-first. See their current invoice attached.

Quick thoughts from my side: we strongly prefer the portal for onboarding (single source of truth, idempotency tokens, automated acknowledgements). That said, we can accept emailed invoices as a short-term fallback if the vendor includes the following so our AP ingest can route automatically: 
- Email subject: "Invoice: Redwood PO=<PO#> | Entity=<EntityCode>"
- Invoice header fields: Invoice number, Invoice date, Total amount, Currency, Remit-to name + address, Bank/Wire instructions (if applicable)
- Line-level fields (CSV or embedded table preferred): PO number, PO line, Description, Quantity, Unit price, Line amount, Tax amount, Entity code (one of: RD-NA, RD-EU, RD-LABS)

If they can put all PO lines in one file, that's fine so long as each line has the PO number + entity code and taxes are broken down per entity. For tax/legal reasons we generally need separate receipts per legal entity for final posting — that means if one invoice covers multiple entities we will still need the vendor to supply a per-entity breakdown that we can treat as separate postings. 

I've attached a very small proposed compact CSV template to show the minimum fields we need: proposed_compact_template.csv (stub). Can you confirm the entity codes and whether we require separate invoice PDFs per entity when they email?

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Thanks Jordan — and hi Priyanka. Welcome! A few procurement/finance constraints to call out so we set expectations: 

1) Portal preference: Procurement requires new vendors to complete the Redwood Vendor Onboarding form and go through the vendor portal for production billing. That gives us remit routing, tax classification, and supplier master controls. We will accept emailed invoices during a brief pilot window (2–3 weeks) but prefer portal as the long-term flow.

2) Legal entity / tax treatment: For bookkeeping and VAT/sales tax reasons we need either: 
  a) separate invoice documents per legal entity (preferred), OR
  b) one consolidated invoice with a clear per-entity breakdown (line-level entity code + tax breakdown) plus a cover page that lists totals per legal entity and the tax registration numbers.

3) PO stamping & matching: Please ensure every invoice line has the PO number in the PO column. We require PO stamping (matching) on receipt for automated posting. If you send via email, include the PO number in the subject as Jordan suggested; if via portal the PO association happens automatically.

4) Required fields for email fallback (minimum):
- Invoice number
- Invoice date
- Vendor legal name + remit-to
- Billing currency
- PO number (line-level)
- Entity code (RD-NA / RD-EU / RD-LABS)
- Line net, tax, and gross amounts
- Attach PDF copy of the invoice per legal entity (if consolidated, include per-entity PDF attachments)

5) Onboarding items to finish: W-9 or local tax docs, bank details verification (secure portal or verifiable PDF), and completed vendor onboarding form (we'll send a link and a small how-to). I've attached our PO-to-entity mapping doc which shows how PO prefixes map to entity codes: redwood_po_matrix.pdf (stub).

Operationally, if Acme can deliver a consolidated CSV with those line-level columns plus a per-entity PDF for posting, we can process the invoices without a hard portal requirement for the pilot. After 3 weeks we will require portal-only for production.

Next step: Priyanka — can you reply with one sample CSV using the column headers below and attach a PDF(s) for the same invoice? We'll validate mapping and confirm go-live date.

Minimum CSV headers (case-insensitive): invoice_number, invoice_date, po_number, po_line, entity_code, description, qty, unit_price, line_net, tax_amount, line_gross, currency

Processing SLA during pilot: 10 business days from receipt with correct mapping. After portal: 7 business days.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Procurement Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
